business_model.basis: Stated directly in the 10-Q MD&A key-terms section and the 10-K Business section.
business_model.claim: Match Group earns revenue from two sources: Direct Revenue (subscriptions and à la carte purchases from end users) and Indirect Revenue (substantially all advertising).
quotes: Direct Revenue is revenue that is received directly from end users of our services and includes both subscription and à la carte revenue.
Indirect Revenue is revenue that is not received directly from an end user of our services, substantially all of which is advertising revenue.
In addition to direct revenue from our users, we generate indirect revenue from advertising, which comprises a much smaller percentage of our overall revenue as compared to direct revenue.

business_model.claim: As of Q2 2026, Match Group reports three operating segments: Tinder, Hinge, and Everyone Everywhere (which combined the former Evergreen & Emerging and MG Asia segments).
quotes: During the quarter ended June 30, 2026, we reorganized our brands into three operating segments. Specifically, the Evergreen and Emerging and MG Asia operating segments were combined into a new segment called "Everyone Everywhere." This change has been reflected in all historical periods presented. The Tinder and Hinge operating segments remain unchanged.

business_model.basis: Stated in the 10-Q and 10-K MD&A key-terms sections.
business_model.claim: Revenue is driven by two metrics: Payers (unique monthly users from whom Direct Revenue is earned) and Revenue Per Payer (RPP, the average monthly Direct Revenue per Payer).
quotes: Payers are unique users at a brand level in a given month from whom we earned Direct Revenue.

Revenue Per Payer ("RPP") is the average monthly revenue earned from a Payer and is Direct Revenue for a period divided by the Payers in the period, further divided by the number of months in the period.

business_model.basis: Stated in the 10-K Business and Risk Factors sections.
business_model.claim: The company operates a freemium model: core features are free, and users pay for premium subscriptions or à la carte features to access enhanced functionality.
quotes: Tinder employs a freemium model, through which users are allowed to enjoy many of the core features of Tinder for free, including limited use of the Swipe Right® feature with unlimited communication with other users. However, to enjoy premium features, such as unlimited use of the Swipe Right® feature or the ability to "See Who Likes You", a Tinder user must subscribe to one of several subscription offerings: Tinder Plus®, Tinder Gold®, or Tinder Platinum®.
Most of our brands monetize via a freemium model where the use of the service is free and a subset of the users pay for subscriptions or in-app purchases to access premium features.

business_model.basis: Stated in the 10-Q MD&A and 10-K MD&A.
business_model.claim: Cost of revenue is driven primarily by in-app purchase fees paid to Apple and Google, variable expenses (hosting, credit-card processing, data-center costs), and employee compensation for data-center and customer-care staff.
quotes: Cost of revenue consists primarily of the amortization of in-app purchase fees, Variable Expenses (defined below), and employee compensation expense and stock-based compensation expense for personnel engaged in data center and customer care functions.

In-app purchase fees consists of the amortization of in-app purchase fees, which are monies paid to Apple and Google in connection with the processing of in-app purchases of subscriptions and service features through the in-app payment systems provided by Apple and Google.
Variable Expenses consists primarily of hosting fees, credit card processing fees, and rent, energy, and bandwidth costs associated with data centers.

business_model.claim: Selling and marketing expense is driven primarily by cost of acquisition (advertising spend across online and offline channels) and employee compensation for marketing personnel.
quotes: Selling and marketing expense consists primarily of cost of acquisition expense and employee compensation expense and stock-based compensation expense for personnel engaged in selling and marketing, sales support, and public relations functions.

Cost of acquisition consists primarily of advertising expenditures, including online marketing (fees paid to search engines and social media sites), offline marketing, including television and print advertising, and production of advertising content.

business_model.claim: International revenue represented 56% of total revenue in fiscal year 2025, and the company varies pricing by local market with revenue typically earned in local currencies.
quotes: Our international revenue represented 56% and 54% of our total revenue for the years ended December 31, 2025 and 2024, respectively. We vary our pricing to align with local market conditions and our international businesses typically earn revenue in local currencies.

business_model.basis: Stated in the 10-K MD&A (In-App Purchase Fees trend) and 10-K Business section.
business_model.claim: The company is required to pay Apple and Google a meaningful share of in-app transaction revenue—generally up to 30% on iOS and 15% on Android—making platform fees a significant and ongoing cost.
quotes: Where users make in-app purchases using Apple's or Google's payment systems, we are required to pay Apple and Google, as applicable, a meaningful share (for subscribers, generally up to 30% on iOS and 15% on Android) of the revenue we receive from these transactions.
We pay Apple and Google a meaningful share of the revenue we receive from in-app transactions as well as where payments on Android and iOS devices are processed through alternative payment systems.

business_model.basis: Stated in the 10-Q MD&A and confirmed in the 10-Q income statement.
business_model.claim: Q3 2026 total revenue of $891,232 (table in thousands) declined 3% Y/Y, with Tinder Direct Revenue down 2%, Hinge up 19%, and Everyone Everywhere down 20% (including a $20 million Azar revenue decrease from the Apple App Store removal and required app redesign).
quotes: Tinder Direct Revenue declined 2%, driven by a 4% decrease in Payers, partially offset by an increase in RPP of 2%.

Hinge Direct Revenue grew 19%, driven by 23% Payer growth, reflecting Hinge's continued European expansion, partially offset by a decrease in RPP of 3% to $31.81 as a result of the expansion of discount optimizations and testing of a new lower priced subscription tier.
E&E Direct Revenue declined 20%, including a $20 million decrease in revenue at Azar resulting from the changes discussed in the Azar business update above.

business_model.basis: Stated in the 10-Q MD&A (Azar Business Update) and 10-K Risk Factors.
business_model.claim: The Azar app was removed from the Apple App Store on February 22, 2026, reinstated on April 6, 2026 after a redesign, and the redesign resulted in lower monetization; a $25.2 million impairment was recorded on the Azar trade name in Q1 2026.
quotes: On February 22, 2026, Apple removed the Azar app from the Apple App Store following a February 6, 2026 update to Apple's App Review Guidelines. Updates were subsequently made to the app to comply with the updated guidelines, which led to the reinstatement of a new version on April 6, 2026. The app updates necessitated by the new guidelines resulted in lower monetization from the new app.

During the quarter ended March 31, 2026, we also updated the business forecast associated with the Azar app, which resulted in an impairment of $25.2 million to the indefinite-lived asset associated with the Azar trade name, which was reclassified to a definite-lived intangible asset as of March 31, 2026.

quotes: A large portion of customers use multiple services over a given period of time, either concurrently or sequentially, reflecting the various ways in which users seek connection, making our broad portfolio of brands a competitive advantage.

quotes: Tinder®, launched in 2012, rose to scale and popularity faster than any other service in the online dating category.
Daily Active Users returned to Y/Y growth in September for the first time in three and a half years.

Hinge Delivered Double-Digit User, Revenue, and Payer Growth Y/Y

competitive_position.basis: Stated in 10-K Business (P1) and Risk Factors (P2).
competitive_position.claim: The social-connection app market is fragmented globally with no single dominant brand, and Match Group competes with large social-media and technology platforms that can leverage their existing user bases to attract connection-app users.
quotes: the market for social connection apps is fragmented, and no single service has been able to effectively serve all of those seeking social connections

We compete with a number of other companies that provide technologies for people to meet each other, including other online dating platforms; social media platforms and social-discovery apps, such as Facebook and Instagram (both owned by Meta), Snap, TikTok, X, LinkedIn (owned by Microsoft), Twitch (owned by Amazon), and YouTube (owned by Alphabet)

competitive_position.claim: Low switching costs and the propensity of consumers to use multiple services simultaneously create a persistent threat that new entrants or a new technology (such as generative AI) could rapidly gain scale at the expense of existing brands.
quotes: costs for consumers to switch between services are low, and consumers have a propensity to try new approaches to connecting with people and to use multiple services at the same time

It is possible that a new service could gain rapid scale at the expense of existing brands through harnessing a new technology, such as generative AI, or a new or existing distribution channel, creating a new or different approach to connecting people, introducing a new business model, or some other means.

competitive_position.basis: Stated in 10-K Business (P1), Risk Factors (P2), and Q3 2026 10-Q MD&A (P4).
competitive_position.claim: Match Group is heavily dependent on the Apple App Store and Google Play Store for distribution and monetization, and Apple's unilateral removal of the Azar app in February 2026 demonstrated the material risk this dependency poses.
quotes: We rely on the Apple App Store and the Google Play Store to distribute and monetize our mobile applications.

on February 22, 2026, Apple removed our Azar app from the Apple App Store following a February 6, 2026 update to Apple's App Review Guidelines, meaning the app is no longer available for download from the Apple App Store.

competitive_position.claim: Total consolidated Payers declined 5% Y/Y in Q3 2026 (13,789 thousand vs 14,527 thousand), and the Everyone Everywhere segment saw a 20% Y/Y revenue decline, reflecting weakness across the non-Tinder, non-Hinge brands.
quotes: E&E Direct Revenue declined 20%, including a $20 million decrease in revenue at Azar resulting from the changes discussed in the Azar business update above. Additional decreases occurred across most brands within E&E as a result of Payer declines.

competitive_position.basis: Stated in Q3 2026 10-Q income statement (F2) and earnings release (P6); table scale is $ in Thousands.
competitive_position.claim: Match Group generated $891,232 thousand in Q3 2026 revenue and $268,569 thousand in operating income, with a 30% operating margin, and nine-month revenue of $2,608,271 thousand, underscoring its scale in the fragmented dating-app market.

competitive_position.basis: Stated in 10-K Business (P1) and Risk Factors (P2).
competitive_position.claim: The company's freemium monetization model, in which most users access core features free and a subset pay for subscriptions or à la carte features, makes financial performance highly sensitive to user retention and conversion rates.
quotes: Most of our brands monetize via a freemium model where the use of the service is free and a subset of the users pay for subscriptions or in-app purchases to access premium features.
If we fail to retain existing users or add new users, or if our users do not convert to paying users, our revenue, financial results, and business may be significantly harmed.

competitive_position.basis: Stated in 10-K Risk Factors (P2) and 10-K MD&A (P3); Q3 2026 improvement noted in P6.
competitive_position.claim: Demand for online dating services has softened among younger generations, particularly women, and Match Group's 2025 portfolio-strategy shift to improve user outcomes (especially for women) is expected to cause short-term revenue and user declines while aiming for long-term growth.
quotes: In recent years, demand for online dating services has softened among younger generations, particularly among women in those generations, reflecting evolving preferences, shifting social behaviors, and changing expectations regarding digital interactions.

in 2025, we shifted our overall portfolio strategy to place greater emphasis on improving user outcomes, particularly for women, with the goal of driving long-term revenue growth. This strategy includes introducing new features and experiences that we believe will improve user outcomes, some of which have in the past and in the future may again drive short-term decreases in both revenue and user numbers.

competitive_position.claim: The company's Google in-app purchase partnership, entered in 2024, is set to expire in Q1 2027, after which fees paid to Google for Android transactions are expected to increase unless Google reduces its standard fees.
quotes: our partnership with Google entered into in 2024 is set to expire in the first quarter of 2027. If Google does not reduce its standard in-app purchase fees, whether voluntarily or involuntarily, before that partnership expires, we expect that the fees paid to Google for transactions processed either through their in-app payment system or through alternative payment options on Android, will increase.
